review_notes: I read the whole file. It has one new definition, `baseChangeTowerBialgEquiv`, plus several private and public lemmas. Mathlib's `Bialgebra/TensorProduct.lean` and `Coalgebra/TensorProduct.lean` have no tower or cancel-base-change bialgebra equivalence. The closest Mathlib declaration is `Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Maps.lean`), which is only an algebra equivalence and needs commutative `A`/`B`. The file builds the bialgebra version with `BialgEquiv.ofAlgEquiv` on top of `TauCeti.Algebra.TensorProduct.baseChangeTowerAlgEquiv`. That algebra equivalence is in another file. Its docstring says it also covers noncommutative `A`, which is a stated reason for it to exist next to the Mathlib one. The remaining declarations are theorems about the equivalence or about the Mathlib bialgebra structure on `T ⊗[R] G`. Standalone theorem duplication is excluded by the rubric. I did not check the other Tau Ceti files for duplicated constructions. I found no competing structure or definition that duplicates a Mathlib concept.
